---
title: "Benchmark: how writes grow with the data"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = TRUE)
results <- function(name) {
  path <- file.path("..", "..", "bench", "results", paste0(name, ".parquet"))
  tibble::as_tibble(arrow::read_parquet(path, mmap = FALSE))
}
scale <- results("scale")
bench_script <- file.path("..", "..", "bench", "scale.R")
(knitr::read_chunk)(bench_script)
has_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
gb <- function(x) round(x / 1024^3, 2)
by_size <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(scale, paste(scale$kind, scale$rows)), function(d) {
  data.frame(
    kind = d$kind[[1]], rows = d$rows[[1]], reps = nrow(d),
    median_s = stats::median(d$seconds), min_s = min(d$seconds), max_s = max(d$seconds),
    s_per_1e6 = stats::median(d$seconds_per_1e6_rows),
    geocode_s = stats::median(d$step_geocode_s), sort_s = stats::median(d$step_sort_s),
    serialise_s = stats::median(d$step_serialise_s), check_s = stats::median(d$step_check_s),
    x_gb = gb(d$x_bytes[[1]]), sim_peak_gb = gb(d$sim_peak_rss_bytes[[1]]),
    rss_before_gb = gb(d$rss_before_bytes[d$rep == 1]),
    peak_gb = gb(d$peak_rss_bytes[d$rep == 1]), increase_gb = gb(d$rss_increase_bytes[d$rep == 1]),
    memory_over_x = d$memory_over_x[d$rep == 1], peak_any_gb = gb(max(d$peak_rss_bytes)),
    staging_gb = gb(max(d$staging_peak_bytes)), store_gb = gb(d$store_bytes[[1]]),
    files = d$files[[1]], sim_s = d$sim_s[[1]]
  )
}))
by_size <- by_size[order(by_size$kind, by_size$rows), ]
```

This article reads stored results; it does not run the benchmark. The script
is `bench/scale.R`; its code is shown below as it was run.

## Question

How do the time, the memory and the staging disk of `store_write()` grow
with the number of rows, from 1e5 to 5e6 polygons? Tables are measured
alongside for comparison.

## Setup

```{r}
env <- scale[1, grep("^env_", names(scale))]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  item = sub("^env_", "", names(env)),
  value = vapply(env, function(v) as.character(v[[1]]), character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
))
```

`rcs_sim_polygons()` written with `partition = "h3"` and `rcs_sim_table()`
written with its key and `partition = "year"`, into a new local store for
every repetition, one geocoding worker. Each size runs in its own R process
(a mirai daemon) that makes the data and writes it; the benchmark's own
process samples the daemon's resident memory and the size of the staging
folder every 0.2 s during each write. Memory is reported as the increase of
resident memory during the write over the memory held just before it (the
data `x` and the loaded packages), and against the size of `x` in memory
(`object.size()`). Steps are timed as in `benchmark-write.Rmd`.

```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r worker, eval = FALSE}

## Results

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  by_size[c("kind", "rows", "reps", "median_s", "min_s", "max_s", "s_per_1e6", "geocode_s", "sort_s", "serialise_s", "check_s")],
  row.names = FALSE, digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

`s_per_1e6` is the median time per million rows; constant values mean
linear growth.

```{r}
knitr::kable(
  by_size[c("kind", "rows", "x_gb", "sim_peak_gb", "rss_before_gb", "peak_gb", "increase_gb", "memory_over_x", "peak_any_gb", "staging_gb", "store_gb", "files")],
  row.names = FALSE, digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Sizes in GiB. Memory columns are those of the first repetition, which
starts in a process that has only made the data: `rss_before_gb` is the
resident memory just before the write, `peak_gb` the largest resident memory
during it, `increase_gb` the difference and `memory_over_x` that difference
divided by `x_gb`. `peak_any_gb` is the largest resident memory over all
repetitions (R keeps freed memory, so later repetitions start higher), and
`sim_peak_gb` that of making the data with `rcs_sim_*()`. `staging_gb` is
the largest size of the staging folder during a write, `store_gb` the size
of the written files.

```{r, eval = has_ggplot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Two log-log line charts against the number of rows, for polygons and tables: the median write time in seconds, and the peak increase of memory in GiB. Both grow roughly in proportion to the number of rows."}
library(ggplot2)
long <- rbind(
  data.frame(kind = by_size$kind, rows = by_size$rows, measure = "write time, s", value = by_size$median_s),
  data.frame(kind = by_size$kind, rows = by_size$rows, measure = "memory increase, GiB", value = by_size$increase_gb)
)
ggplot(long, aes(x = rows, y = value, colour = kind)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Rows (log scale)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Verdict

```{r, include = FALSE}
poly <- by_size[by_size$kind == "polygons", ]
tab <- by_size[by_size$kind == "table", ]
largest <- poly[which.max(poly$rows), ]
```

- Time grows about linearly: from
  `r round(poly$s_per_1e6[[1]])` to `r round(largest$s_per_1e6)` seconds per
  million polygons between `r format(min(poly$rows), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
  and `r format(largest$rows, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` rows;
  geocoding stays the largest part
  (`r round(100 * largest$geocode_s / largest$median_s)`% at
  `r format(largest$rows, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` rows); the
  choice of the H3 partition resolution, counted in "sort", works on the
  distinct cells and takes
  `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * largest$sort_s / largest$median_s)`%.
- Tables grow linearly too, but the serialization check grows with the
  number of files: it reads one whole row group of every file (about half
  a second each for the simulated table) before it compares the sampled
  rows, so it took
  `r round(100 * tab$check_s[which.max(tab$rows)] / tab$median_s[which.max(tab$rows)])`%
  of the write of `r format(max(tab$rows), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`
  rows in `r tab$files[which.max(tab$rows)]` files.
- Memory: from 1e6 rows on, a polygon write needs at most
  `r sprintf("%.2f", max(poly$memory_over_x[poly$rows >= 1e6]))` times the size of
  `x` on top of `x` itself (`r largest$increase_gb` GiB for
  `r format(largest$rows, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)` polygons of
  `r largest$x_gb` GiB), and a table write at most
  `r sprintf("%.2f", max(tab$memory_over_x[tab$rows >= 1e6]))` times. Small writes
  show larger ratios (up to `r round(max(by_size$memory_over_x), 1)`)
  because fixed costs (Arrow buffers, loaded code) weigh more.
- Staging disk is about the size of the written files (the largest staging
  folder was `r largest$staging_gb` GiB for files of `r largest$store_gb` GiB):
  the files are staged once and copied.

## Limits

- One machine with `r env$env_ram_gb` GB of RAM. The sizes 1e5, 1e6 and 5e6
  were measured again on the quiet machine after the speed fixes of the
  fourth wave, with three, three and one repetitions (column `reps`); the
  rows of 5e5 and 2e6 polygons are those of the first run, before those
  fixes and on a machine that ran other agents, and are kept for the shape
  of the curve.
- Resident memory is sampled every 0.2 s, so a peak shorter than that can be
  missed; R also returns freed memory to the system late, so the
  "before" level of later repetitions is higher than that of the first.
- Local store only; the upload to a cloud bucket adds time but no memory
  (files are streamed from the staging folder).
